corpus.note: The SAME corpus as `pydantic`, file for file. It exists only so that hand-written queries can be compared with LLM-drafted ones while everything else is held still. Its chunk vectors are a copy of pydantic's, which is exact because the file set is identical.
corpus.include_note: Identical to the `pydantic` fixture. Do not change one without the other or the comparison stops being paired.
corpus.why: Written question-first: each question was written from what a pydantic user would want to know, then its answer was located with grep. No model was involved. They use ordinary DOMAIN vocabulary (json schema, alias, enum, immutable) but never an identifier copied out of the answer - which is the line corpora.leaked() draws, and the line a first attempt at this fixture got wrong by banning plain words too and scoring an unfairly low MRR of 0.101.

fields.query: the question, written BEFORE its answer was located
fields.expects: line numbers in that file that answer it
